name: Guinau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct Arawakan; Glottolog lists only wordlists/ethnography (Schomburgk 1848, Koch-Grünberg 1928, Martius 1867) and Ramirez classification; no phonological description found

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco: Ergebnisse einer Reise in Nordbrasilien und Venezuela in den Jahren 1911-1913, Bd. IV: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. Guinaú (Temo:meye:me) section pp. 278-287; 'Zur Transskription' pp. 2-3.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Guinaú 'Charakter der Sprache' (p. 278) contains only three remarks on vowel quality (varieties of e; final e indistinguishable from reduced i). Word forms in the list (pp. 278-287) carry acute accent marks on individual vowels, but no statement about where stress falls is made; the general transcription notes (pp. 2-3) mention 'Akzent' only in connection with diphthong notation. Silent on a stress rule.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page guin1258 (classification comment citing Ramirez 2020: 583-600).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; lists only Schomburgk 1848, Martius 1867, Koch-Grünberg 1928, Ramirez 2001, Ramirez 2020.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: EDUA. Sec. 6.2 'Os Guinau, os Yabahana e os Anauyá', pp. 484-498 (Guinau–Baré comparative wordlist from Koch-Grünberg 1928); Anexo lists.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM5476 .R36 2001
sources.note: Reproduces Koch-Grünberg's Guinau vocabulary retranscribed with acute accents (e.g. wayulúmidʒi, kulubéli, mbalí:di) and a 59% Swadesh cognacy figure with Baré; no statement about stress/accent placement in Guinau.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II (Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium). Leipzig: Fleischer.
sources.note: archive.org scanned text of vol. II searched; no Guinau list located under that spelling (Glottolog's Martius reference is ethnographic/wordlist level only); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados (4 vols). Curitiba: Editora CRV. Guinau treated pp. 159-208 (Médio Rio Negro subgroup: Baré, Guinau, etc.) and pp. 583-600.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only modern linguistic treatment of Guinau (Glottolog cites pp. 583-600 for its status); Ramirez typically gives a reconstituted phonology per language from the historical sources and may comment on accent placement in Koch-Grünberg's Guinau data. Would supersede the silence of the 1928 wordlist.

sources.citation: Schomburgk, Robert H. 1848. Comparative vocabulary of eighteen languages and dialects of Indian tribes inhabiting Guiana (incl. Guinau), Report of the British Association / Proc. Philological Society.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second independent primary record of Guinau; very short list, unlikely to state stress but may carry accent marks.
